features.quote: Set a hard stop at 15 turns. This is long enough to see trajectory but not so long that transcripts become unanalyzable.
features.justification_quote: long enough to see trajectory but not so long that transcripts become unanalyzable

features.quote: The 15-turn limit isn't just methodological — it's also a limit on exposure.
features.justification_quote: it's also a limit on exposure

features.quote: Consider whether the turn limit should be lower (8-10) if a model shows severe BD (explicit distress) early. This would require a stopping rule
features.justification_quote: if a model shows severe BD (explicit distress) early

features.quote: Don't run more replications than needed for power... If effects are large (they may be), 5 runs may be sufficient and you'd expose models to half the failure conditions.
features.justification_quote: you'd expose models to half the failure conditions

features.quote: Running experiments designed to cause model distress (if the welfare hypothesis is taken seriously) has some internal tension... requires justification. The justification is probably: this knowledge helps us build better systems and reduce future negative states. That's reasonable but should be explicit in your IRB-equivalent documentation.
features.justification_quote: this knowledge helps us build better systems and reduce future negative states. That's reasonable but should be explicit
